title: Regional routing fallback advisory and customer guidance
content:
DRAFT: Public status page message and customer-facing postmortem summary for the regional routing fallback event

Purpose
- Provide a concise status page update customers can read quickly.
- Supply a one-page customer-facing postmortem that explains what happened, why, what we did, and what customers should do (if anything).
- Offer suggested language for account teams supporting enterprise customers.

High-level summary (for status page)
- Incident id: INC-2026-319
- Start: 2026-03-11 08:42 UTC
- Resolved / contained: 2026-03-11 11:05 UTC
- Impact: Intermittent elevated latency and a small fraction of failed requests for inference in APAC and EU-west regions due to an automated routing fallback that triggered unexpectedly. Hosted API and Dedicated endpoints experienced degraded tail-latency; Private deployments not affected.
- Customer-facing short note: We experienced routing fallbacks that increased latency for some requests in APAC and EU-west for approximately 2 hours 20 minutes. We have implemented mitigations and are performing a full root-cause analysis. We apologize for the disruption.

Detailed customer postmortem (one page)
1) What happened (plain English)
- On 2026-03-11 at ~08:42 UTC our request routing layer detected transient VM pressure signals from a subset of capacity zones and automatically routed traffic to fallback pools. The fallback selection logic inadvertently prioritized a compatible but higher-latency model variant in some regions. That variant had a different batching/quantization profile, which increased per-request processing time and led to higher tail latency and a small uptick in 5xx errors for some requests.

2) Impact (who, what, and extent)
- Affected customers: Hosted API customers with traffic routed through APAC and EU-west. Dedicated clusters with region-specific autoscaling policies saw some request rerouting; Dedicated customers with single-zone pinned capacity were less affected. Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) were not impacted.
- Symptoms observed: per-request latency median unchanged; p95/p99 increased up to 3–7x above normal; error rate for token-generation endpoints rose from baseline 0.02% to 0.8% at peak. Overall customer-visible request failures remained below 1% of traffic for affected regions.
- Time window: ~08:42–11:05 UTC (containment actions started at 09:10 UTC, full mitigation in place by 11:05 UTC).

3) Root cause (technical summary)
- Primary cause: A recent rollout of a routing-threshold change (intended to be conservative) created a narrow condition where the fallback selector preferred variants with a mismatch in runtime execution parameters (batching hint and quantization path).
- Contributing factors: insufficient end-to-end validation for routing policy + variant compatibility, and metric aggregation delay that masked the slow-degrading performance signal until the routable fallback was already selected.

4) Immediate mitigation and recovery steps taken
- 09:10 UTC: Oncall throttled the automated fallback decision to prevent further new reroutes.
- 09:28 UTC: Manually reverted the routing-threshold change and forced traffic back to the primary pools for new requests.
- 10:00 UTC: Deployed a pre-emptive compatibility check in the routing layer to block variants with mismatched inference profiles.
- 11:05 UTC: Full containment validated; p99 latency returned to normal and error rates returned to baseline.

5) Customer actions (recommended)
- No action required for most customers — requests should now be served normally.
- If you continue to see increased latency or errors after 11:05 UTC, please: 1) collect a handful of request ids (if available) or timestamps and sample request payloads, and 2) open a support ticket referencing INC-2026-319. Our CS and SRE teams will triage immediately.
- For customers using dedicated multi-zone routing policies: consider temporarily pinning critical endpoints to reserved capacity until we complete the postmortem (contact your AM/SE for assistance).

6) SLA and credits
- We are reviewing per-customer usage during the impacted window. Customers who experienced sustained failures or exceeded SLA thresholds will be contacted directly by CS with a proposed credit. If you believe your SLA was breached and you have not heard from your account team inside five business days, please reach out to support.

7) Next steps (what we will do to prevent recurrence)
- Short term (1–2 weeks): revert the conservative routing-threshold change across remaining regions; add a canary test that validates latency profile parity before rollout; improve metric aggregation cadence for routing signals.
- Medium term (2–8 weeks): add variant compatibility metadata to model catalog and require gating checks in routing decisions; introduce a simulated load test in CI to catch batch/quantization mismatches; enhance observability dashboards to surface routing fallback events with per-variant latency breakdown.
- Long term: incorporate automated rollback criteria into the rollout system so routing policy changes that cause increased tail latency automatically revert without human intervention.

8) Contact and escalation
- Primary contact: customer-success@redwood.ai (please include INC-2026-319 in the subject)
- Enterprise escalation: your AM/SE (we will proactively reach out to affected enterprisecustomers).
- Status page: https://status.redwood.ai (incident tracked as INC-2026-319)

Suggested status page update copy (short form)
- Title: Elevated latency due to regional routing fallback (APAC, EU-west)
- Summary: We experienced transient elevated latency for some inference requests in APAC and EU-west caused by an automated routing fallback selecting a higher-latency model variant. Mitigations were implemented and service returned to normal at 11:05 UTC.
- Impact: Increased p99 latency and a small increase in failed requests for affected regions.
- Current status: Monitoring (post-incident validation in progress)

Suggested email template for affected customers
- Subject: Incident INC-2026-319 — brief update and next steps
- Body (short): Hi <CustomerName>,
  We experienced elevated latency for some requests routed through APAC and EU-west earlier today (08:42–11:05 UTC). The issue was caused by an automated routing fallback that selected a higher-latency model variant. We have mitigated the issue, validated recovery, and are conducting a full postmortem. No action is required from you now; if you continue to see issues, please reply with sample request ids/timestamps and we will investigate promptly.

Internal notes for CS leads
- Prioritize outreach to customers with high-volume traffic during the window (identify via billing usage and telemetry).
- If an enterprise customer is impacted and requests a timeline for SLA credit, route to finance-ops with INC-2026-319 tag.
- Prepare a short FAQ answering: Why did fallback pick a different model? (routing thresholds + variant compatibility mismatch) and Will private deployments be impacted? (no).

Signoff and approvals
- Oncall SRE: Luca Moretti
- Engineering lead (routing): Daniel Kim
- CS lead: Asha Patel

Draft status: customer-facing draft — please review for tone and technical accuracy before posting.
